label: Argo (two-stage sounding rocket)
description: Generic two-stage research rocket: 80 mm booster on a Cesaroni 1364K454, 56 mm sustainer on a Cesaroni 659J381. Passive staging: drag separation at booster burnout, sustainer ignites 1.0 s later. The booster recovers on its own chute (motor ejection charge); the sustainer flies dual deploy. Not modelled on any real vehicle.

notes.booster: 1.1 kg airframe (80 mm tube, 4 fins, interstage), Cd 0.80 alone: open, blunt front end
notes.sustainer: 1.0 kg (56 mm fiberglass, 38 mm mount, avionics), Cd 0.42 with Mach model
notes.stack_cd: 0.55 with Mach model: the stack is longer and has the interstage transition
notes.separation: ballistic coefficient m/(Cd A) ~ 400 kg/m^2 (booster) vs ~1600 (sustainer): the booster decelerates ~4x harder and falls away without a separation charge
notes.ignition_delay: 1.0 s: long enough for clean separation, short enough not to bleed speed
notes.booster_recovery: 36 in chute on the K454's 10 s ejection delay (near booster apogee)
notes.backup: sustainer motor flown plugged: the J381's longest delay (15 s) fires at 21.0 s, ~4 s BEFORE the 25.3 s true apogee. Independent timer at 28.5 s after first ignition: after the latest dispersed apogee (25.9 s) and after the FC's own 26.9 s backup timer.
notes.sustainer_recovery: dual deploy: 24 in drogue at apogee, 48 in main at 300 m
notes.expected_band: reported K-to-J two-stage high-power flights reach roughly 12-20 kft (3.7-6 km). The first hand estimate (4-12 km) came from ideal delta-v and ignored supersonic drag, which the Mach model shows dominates (a lighter sustainer flies LOWER); revised to this documented range.

notes.backup_timer_s: nominal true apogee + max(1.0 s, 4 sigma of the apogee time under the standard dispersions), from lift-off; the C6 value 8.5 s follows the same rule (7.42 + 1.08)
notes.max_boost_s: longest burn x 1.6 (C6: 1.86 s -> 3.0 s): burnout fallback for a stuck accelerometer
notes.min_deploy_after_launch_s: final burnout x 1.35 (C6: 1.86 s -> 2.5 s): deploy inhibit
notes.basis: booster K454 burns 3.15 s, sustainer J381 1.87 s after a 1.0 s gap (final burnout 6.02 s); true apogee 25.28 s (sigma 0.41 s); peak ~28 g
notes.burns: 2: after the first burnout the FC waits (deployment locked out, no gating) for the sustainer; ignition = accel > 20 m/s^2 for 5 samples
notes.stage_ignition_timeout_s: 2.0 s = 1.0 s ignition delay + ~0.1 s detection + 0.9 s margin; if the sustainer never lights the FC continues as a single-stage coast and still deploys at apogee
notes.sensors: ADXL375-class +-200 g accelerometer (sigma 1.0 m/s^2, bias 0.5 m/s^2): the motor's peak specific force exceeds the hobby sensor's +-24 g, which would clip most of the burn and corrupt the filter's velocity by hundreds of m/s. The filter's R, full scale and reference gate are derived from this model.
notes.main: FC commands the main at 300 m; backup timer device at 28.5 s backs up the drogue
notes.powered_jerk_psd: 1e4 m^2/s^5 under thrust and for 0.5 s after each detected burnout (tail-off): the coast q (10) cannot follow thrust-curve and tail-off jerk on this rocket, the gate then rejected genuine samples and nominal flights went 'inconsistent' (found by the fleet SIL runs; see fc/include/fc/config.hpp). 1e4 sits in the measured plateau: apogee detection +0.04-0.05 s on every preset
notes.kf.jerk_psd: 1000 m^2/s^5 in coast (vs 10 for the subsonic rockets): this rocket coasts supersonically and decelerates through the transonic drag rise, where the true acceleration changes at up to ~95 m/s^3 (measured), about 6x the subsonic C6's coast jerk. With q=10 the gate rejected those genuine changes on hot-motor dispersed flights (fleet campaign). Scaling q with jerk^2 gives ~350; 1000 adds margin and sits in the measured plateau (M3: same accuracy up to 1000).
